{{primary|date=June 2020}}
The '''Joan & Joseph Birman Research Prize in Topology and Geometry''' is a prize given every other year by the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] to an outstanding young female researcher in [[topology]] or [[geometry]]. The prize fund for the award was endowed by a donation in 2013 from [[Joan Birman]] and her husband, [[Joseph Birman]], and first awarded in 2015.

== Winners ==
* [[Elisenda Grigsby]] (2015), for her research in low-dimensional [[topology]], particularly in [[knot theory]] and categorified invariants.{{r|grigsby}}{{r|grigsby2}}{{r|grigsby3}}
* [[Emmy Murphy]] (2017), for her research in [[symplectic geometry]] where she developed new techniques for studying [[symplectic manifold]]s and [[contact geometry]].{{r|murphy}}{{r|murphy2}}
* [[Kathryn Mann]] (2019), for "major breakthroughs in the theory of dynamics of group actions on manifolds".{{r|mann}}
* [[Emily Riehl]] (2021), for "deep and foundational work in category theory and homotopy theory".<ref>{{Cite web|last=|first=|date=|title=Joan and Joseph Birman Research Prize 2021|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-birman-research-prize/awm-birman-research-prize-2021/|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=|website=}}</ref>
* [[Kristen Hendricks]] (2023), for "highly influential work on equivariant aspects of Floer homology theories".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://awm-math.org/awards/awm-birman-research-prize/awm-birman-research-prize-2023/|title=Joan and Joseph Birman Research Prize 2023|publisher=Association for Women in Mathematics|access-date=2023-05-20}}</ref>
* [[Mona Merling]] (2025), for "innovative and impactful research in algebraic K-theory, equivariant homotopy theory, and their applications to manifold theory".<ref>{{Cite web |title=Notices of the AMS |url=https://www.ams.org/journals/notices/202411/rnoti-p1543.pdf |access-date=2025-04-04 |website=American Mathematical Society (AMS) |language=en-US}}</ref>
